A total of only ~27KB transferred across the whole flow (2646 IN_BYTES + 24694 OUT_BYTES) is far too small to exhaust bandwidth or resources, with the response-heavy split matching a normal data delivery.
A 24 ms transient burst ending in a normal close is a single short transaction, not a sustained flood characteristic of denial-of-service activity.
TTL of 31-32 (MAX_TTL 32) is consistent with a genuine unspoofed endpoint roughly 32 hops from a default-TTL-64 host, with no TTL anomaly suggesting forged DoS source addresses.

14 of 44 outbound retransmissions (31.8%) was the strongest counter-signal hinting at congestion or attack, but within a cleanly FIN-closed, low-volume flow it reads as a congested benign session rather than an attack signature.
